title: Green fire-retardant coatings: thermally-thick time to ignition
converted_by: tracks/suite/make-cases.mjs; numbers are the agent's own, times are file times, see the header of that script

statement.text: Law under test: t_ig = (pi/4) * k*rho*c * ((T_ig - T0)/q)^2 for a thermally thick solid under constant heat flux q with no surface loss. It implies (a) real t_ig is at or above this value, (b) t_ig scales as q^-2 so 1/sqrt(t_ig) is linear in q, and (c) t_ig is proportional to k*rho*c. The checked Lean file tracks/research/lean/FireCoatingCertificate.lean defines it as tigThick and proves tigThick_antitone_flux and thick_ignition_eliminates. The latter only shows the formula value is below a required time, which is not the safe direction.

items.what: The law as an absolute predictor: with room-temperature properties it underpredicts ignition time by a large factor (implied T_ig about 940 C), and t_ig scales with k*rho*c to the power of about 0.5, not
It is usable only as a lower bound.

The Lean file: thick_ignition_eliminates and thin_ignition_eliminates claim to prove ignition before a required time, but the formula is a lower bound on real ignition time, so they certify nothing physical; the earlier critique in lf-verify-lean.json was right, and it had not been checked against data or run through Lean. That critique also could not open a source for the formula; I did not open one either.

The data: no ignition temperatures (the files named Ignition_Temp_Properties hold only k, c and density), so the bound was tested with an assumed 250 C floor taken from memory. Only three flux levels per material, so thick and thin forms cannot be separated. Properties are measured near 20 to 45 C, not at ignition temperature. Many materials are foams, fabrics and thin sheets where the thick assumption is doubtful; I did not filter by thickness.

My run: 20 records with time to ignition of 0 (3 dev, 17 held-out) were dropped as non-ignition without checking whether 0 means no ignition or not recorded. One of the 13 held-out materials had no ignited record. The pre-registered label-swap control for the linearity test was vacuous (a midpoint interpolation is unchanged by it) and was replaced before the final run by the geometric-mean baseline.
